question: Acid rain has pH value less than:
solution:
The correct answer is__** 5.6.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acid rain** is caused by the release of **sulfur dioxide **and** nitrogen oxides** into the atmosphere, which react with** water, oxygen,** and other chemicals to form **sulfuric acid, nitric acid, **and other pollutants.
 
• The pH scale ranges from** 0 to 14, with 7 **being **neutral.**
 
• Anything** below 7** is considered **acidic,** and anything** above 7** is considered **basic.**
 
• The pH of acid rain is typically between **4.2 and 5.6**, which is significantly more **acidic** than normal rainwater (pH 5.6-6.5).
 
• Acid rain can have **harmful effects** on the environment, including damaging crops and forests, making bodies of water more acidic, and causing respiratory problems in humans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A pH value of** 8.6 **is actually considered **basic, **not acidic.

 
 
• Water with a pH of 8.6 is slightly alkaline and can be found in some **natural springs and wells**.
 
 
 
• A pH value of **6.6** is still slightly **acidic**, but less so than acid rain.
 
 
• This pH level can be found in some natural bodies of water and is generally **safe for aquatic life.**
 
 
 
• A pH value of **7.6** is **neutral,** not acidic.
 
 
• This pH level can be found in most** tap water **and is safe for **human consumption.**
